item.title: Report: Lower Pricing Made Up 85% of the Estimate Gap on Disputed Property Claims
item.description: Most of the dollar difference between insurer and public adjuster estimates on disputed property claims came from insurers pricing the same repairs lower, according to a new report. According to the report, on 46 disputed claims where both the insurer and the public adjuster itemized the work, lower pricing on repairs that appeared in both estimates accounted for $7.2 million of the $8.5 million difference, or about 85%. Finch Claims’ Q3 2026 State of the Claim Report examines estimates, settlements and payment timelines from a database of 11,530 property claim files handled by public adjusters, with data through Oct.

item.title: FCA proposes greater pension investment flexibility to support long-term value for savers
item.description: Workplace pension providers could have greater flexibility to invest for the long term under proposals from the FCA, helping them deliver better outcomes for savers while ensuring savers' interests remain protected. The proposed change would give providers greater flexibility to access a broader range of investments where this could help improve long-term returns and value for savers. We want providers to have greater choice over how they invest for the long term where this can deliver better outcomes for savers.

item.title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
item.description: While we may cut carbs and fret over fat, most of us are still keen on protein. In response, more recent startup investment has shifted away from meat substitutes and toward stuffing more protein into other packaged foods and drinks. But if they did, protein would surely be this era’s winner.

item.title: How Founders Can Reduce Platform Risk Before It Threatens Growth
item.description: We survived, and this episode taught me that platform dependency is ultimately infrastructure risk. As founders, we prepare for cloud outages and payment failures, but losing access to the platform that brings us customers deserves the same attention. We even reached out to our internal contacts, only for them to tell us that helping us could put their jobs at risk.

item.title: Munich Re’s P&C reinsurance sees decline in Q3, while net result rises to €5.7bn for 9M’26
item.description: Global reinsurer Munich Re has posted a lower net result of €1.742 billion for the third quarter of 2026, and a higher result of €5.667 billion for the first nine months of the year, while the firm’s P&C reinsurance arm saw a notable year-on-year decline as a result of currency and renewal effects. As mentioned, Munich Re says that the year-on-year revenue decline in P&C reinsurance to €12.4 billion for 9M’26 is a result of currency and renewal effects. In addition, Munich Re’s P&C reinsurance business generated a net result of €938 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with €1.187 billion in the prior year period, as insurance revenue from insurance contracts issued increased to €4.446 billion from €4.241 billion in Q3’25.

item.title: SafePoint’s $100m Nature Coast Re 2026-3 industry-loss cat bond price moves to upper-end
item.description: – Nature Coast Re 2026-3 catastrophe bond for SafePoint remains unchanged we are told, with still $100 million of annual aggregate and industry-loss index triggered named storm protection being sought from the capital markets for SafePoint. – Nature Coast Re 2026-3 catastrophe bond deal, but we’re told the price guidance for the notes on offer has moved towards the upper-end of the initial range. As we’ve explained before, this is not the first time SafePoint Insurance Company has ventured to the catastrophe bond market to obtain securitized industry-loss warranty (ILW) type protection.

item.title: California Earthquake Authority lowers pricing again for still $900m Ursa Re 2026-1 cat bond
item.description: The California Earthquake Authority’s (CEA) new Ursa Re Ltd. (Series 2026-1) catastrophe bond remains at the upsized $900 million target, but pricing has been lowered again for the notes on offer, as the company targets strong execution with its latest cat bond deal, Artemis understands. The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) is one of the most consistent sponsors of catastrophe bonds, with this marking the 25th cat bond sponsorship we have tracked from the insurer.

item.title: Talanx 9M’26 net income hits record €2.2bn, supported by reinsurance division
item.description: German insurance and reinsurance group Talanx, the majority shareholder of Hannover Re, reported an improved combined ratio of 89% for the first nine months of 2026, compared with 89.8% a year earlier, as its insurance service result increased by 11% to €4.4 billion and group net income rose by 12% to €2.2 billion. Talanx also recognised €200 million in reinsurance reserves during the second quarter for potential losses associated with the war in Iran. On the investment side, Talanx reported a 52% increase in its net insurance financial and investment result before currency effects to €1.5 billion from €1 billion, supported by its previous shift from lower-yielding to higher-yielding investments and larger realised gains from investment sales.

item.title: Geopolitical risks and AI-driven cyberattacks key risk factors for European re/insurers in 2027: S&P
item.description: Geopolitical risks and AI-driven cyberattacks are set to remain key risk factors for European re/insurers in 2027, according to new commentary from S&P Global Ratings. S&P’s new report has suggested that geopolitical risks affect the European insurance sector mainly indirectly, because policies typically exclude acts of war, including those covering business interruption and transport. However, the European insurers that we rate have taken proactive measures to reduce cyber risk,” the rating agency said.

item.title: US reciprocal insurance exchanges expand as property insurance pressures drive growth, ALIRT finds
item.description: The US reciprocal insurance exchange market has experienced significant growth in recent years, driven by property insurance affordability and availability challenges in catastrophe-exposed regions, according to a new report from ALIRT Insurance Research, a US-based insurance financial research and analysis firm. ALIRT also noted that the reciprocal model is gaining traction beyond property insurance, with new exchanges established to provide personal motor and commercial liability cover. Although the sector remains dominated by a small number of established insurers, ALIRT identified an increase in newly formed exchanges targeting underserved property insurance markets.

item.title: ANZ CEO Matos Warns of Global Jobs Crisis Without AI Rules
item.description: Chief Executive Officer Nuno Matos has called for global regulation to manage the impact of artificial intelligence on the labor market, which he warned could trigger an international crisis. Should large-scale job cuts of up to 50% emerge, “we’ll have a crisis and it’s not going to be in Australia, it’s going to be a global crisis,” Matos said Thursday during a parliamentary hearing in Canberra. “I hope that obviously the world and the administrations are capable of cooperating and ensuring that this technology does not create a social problem at a global level,” Matos said.

item.title: Zurich Insurance Says Europe Storms Drove Catastrophe Losses
item.description: Zurich Insurance Group AG said it saw elevated natural catastrophe losses in its property/casualty business in the third quarter, following storms in Germany, Italy and Switzerland. The period was marked by weather events in Europe including hailstorms and heavy rain, which drove property, vehicle and infrastructure claims. Slower rate increases in the large-property business weighed on commercial insurance, Zurich said.

item.title: At Least 8 Killed, 17 Injured in NYC Multiple-Dwelling Building Collapse
item.description: At least eight people have died and more than 17 including seven children and one firefighter have been injured in a building collapse in Brooklyn. call Wednesday to 1321 Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn for the collapse of a three-story, multiple-dwelling building into an adjacent construction evacuation site. “Multiple people from the building and the construction site were trapped,” FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said during an 8:30 pm press briefing with the mayor and other city officials.

item.title: Mutual of Omaha expands Employee Navigator integration
item.description: Mutual of Omaha has expanded its integration with benefits administration platform Employee Navigator to automate the evidence of insurability (EOI) process for employers offering its insurance products. The connection eliminates manual forms and paperwork, returning decisions and status updates directly through Employee Navigator. “Evidence of insurability has long been one of the last paper-driven steps in benefits enrollment.” – George Reese, CEO of Employee Navigator.

item.title: Erie highlights investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer
item.description: Erie Strategic Ventures , the venture capital arm of Erie Insurance, has highlighted investments in AI software development platform Blitzy and AI security company HiddenLayer . Partnering with Blitzy and HiddenLayer enables our efforts in these areas.” – Keith Kennedy, senior vice president for Next Level Innovation at Erie Insurance. Erie’s backing of Blitzy was previously disclosed in May, when the startup announced a $200 million funding round at a $1.4 billion valuation.

item.title: Accelerant Exchange premium grows 27%
item.description: Accelerant reported $1.33 billion in exchange written premium for the third quarter of 2026, up 27% year over year, as it added 26 MGAs to its specialty insurance platform. Third-party insurers accounted for 49% of exchange written premium, up from 32%, reflecting a growing share of business placed with external carriers. For the first nine months, exchange written premium increased 22% to $3.79 billion, and net income totaled $66.7 million.

item.title: Not in a FEMA Flood Zone? Your Home Could Still Be at Risk
item.description: If your home isn’t in a federally designated flood zone, flooding might seem like someone else’s problem. When these other factors are considered, your home’s true flood risk is far more complex than the map might seem to indicate. Mounting evidence reveals that significantly more homes are at risk of flooding than is indicated by FEMA’s 100-year flood maps – about 6 million more , and 14.6 million properties in all, by one estimate.

item.title: Insurtech Lemonade Posts $43.7M Loss for Q3
item.description: Insurtech Lemonade reported a third quarter 2026 net loss of about $43.7 million compared with a loss of about $37.5 million during the same time in 2025. 30, Lemonade has posted a net loss of $122.9 million compared with a net loss of $143.8 million a year ago. In a letter to shareholders, Lemonade characterized its latest quarterly results as “excellent,” with positive topline growth.

item.title: Policy Disconnects, Deferred Mitigation Escalate Weather-Related Claims
item.description: In response, insurers are tightening policy language, strictly enforcing policy conditions, and scrutinizing claims through a highly analytical lens. The property/casualty insurance industry is operating under unprecedented environmental and financial pressure as the impacts of extreme weather events compound. In January, Winter Storm Fern blasted the country, leaving an estimated $4 billion to $6.7 billion in insured losses and instantly cementing its place as one of the costliest winter weather events since 1950 , Carrier Management reported.

item.title: MAPFRE Raises €1 Billion to Finance Safety Insurance Acquisition
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) MAPFRE (Madrid) has completed €1 billion in debt financing to support its acquisition of Safety Insurance Group (Boston). MAPFRE says both tranches form part of its debt restructuring plan for the acquisition of 100 percent of Safety Insurance Group. Position The acquisition of Safety Insurance Group is intended to strengthen MAPFRE’s presence in the U.S., particularly in New England.

item.title: Zingtree Adds Agentic Governance for Regulated Customer Operations
item.description: (Image source: Zingtree homepage.) Zingtree (San Francisco) has launched an AI governance and orchestration platform designed for customer-service operations in regulated industries including insurance, financial services and healthcare. Iyer says the company sought to preserve its existing rules-based automation while adding greater agentic reasoning and extending those capabilities across customer operations. The platform combines agentic AI with rule-based controls intended to govern how AI agents handle customer interactions and execute actions across enterprise systems.

item.title: American Integrity’s Q3’26 net income surges 115% as policies in-force reach 481k
item.description: American Integrity’s net investment income amounted to $8.4 million, a 21.9% increase from $6.9 million, primarily due to growth in its invested assets, driven by higher in-force premiums. American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc., a Tampa-based property and casualty insurance holding company, has reported net income of $28.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, up 115.4% from $13.2 million in the same period a year earlier. American Integrity attributed the increase to new policies written through the voluntary market and the 2025 Citizens take-outs.

item.title: Marsh names Ed Gold CEO of UK Aviation and Space
item.description: Marsh has confirmed that Ed Gold will become CEO of its UK Aviation and Space business within Marsh Risk from 1 January 2027, according to Reinsurance News. Gold replaces Tony Ambrose, who retains his position as Global Chairman of Aviation and Space and will continue working with clients in an advisory capacity. Gold is currently Deputy CEO of UK Aviation and Space.

item.title: Allstate to launch personal agentic AI assistant in early 2027
item.description: Allstate plans to launch its own personal agentic assistant focused on protection in early 2027, CEO Tom Wilson told analysts on the company's Q3 2026 earnings call on 5 November. It will also serve third-party personal agentic assistants such as Muse. Through Allstate unit Answer Financial, the assistant will be able to review multiple insurance companies at once.

item.title: USAA Bank launches HomeStory-powered real estate service
item.description: USAA has launched Agent Connection , a free service powered by HomeStory that connects members buying or selling homes with vetted real estate agents and offers potential savings at closing. Agent Connection brings together vetted real estate professionals, personalized support and opportunities to save on closing costs, enabling our members to move forward with confidence while keeping more of their hard-earned money.” – Craig Lamp, SVP Lending, USAA Bank. Available to all USAA members, the service includes home search tools and access to HomeStory’s national agent network.

item.title: Ohio Mutual launches CrashBay-powered repair program
item.description: Ohio Mutual has launched its Trusted Repair Program, powered by CrashBay , connecting people involved in auto claims with a vetted repair network and coordinated support from first notice of loss through completed repairs. Announced earlier this year and now available, the program gives Ohio Mutual a shared workflow for managing estimates, supplements, re-inspections and communication with repair shops. Ohio Mutual said the partnership expands repair options while giving its claims team greater visibility into the repair process.

item.title: GEICO opens New York City marketing hub
item.description: GEICO has opened a marketing hub in New York City, adding a space for its marketing team, company leaders and partners to collaborate. “You go to New York City for hustle, for talent and because you want to win,” Lewko wrote. The hub gives GEICO another location to bring together marketing talent and partners.

item.title: Javier Sánchez sustituye a David Alonso como vocal de Adecose por Aon
item.description: La Junta Directiva de Adecose ha aprobado por unanimidad la incorporación de Javier Sánchez como nuevo vocal en representación de Aon, en sustitución de David Alonso, que ocupaba el puesto desde 2019. Sánchez es Co-Head of Affinity, SME & Digital Client Solutions del bróker y miembro de su Comité Ejecutivo.

item.title: FSB recommends Türkiye further strengthens its regulatory framework for crypto-assets and stablecoins
item.description: Building on these achievements, the FSB recommends that Turkish authorities further enhance crypto-asset and stablecoin regulation and supervision by operationalising a framework for financial stability monitoring, establishing a dedicated regime for stablecoins, strengthening supervision and enforcement, and promoting effective cross-border cooperation and information sharing. However, further steps are warranted to reinforce the country’s regulatory framework and improve alignment with the FSB Global Regulatory Framework for Crypto-asset Activities . Press enquiries: +41 61 280 8477 [email protected] Ref: 15/2026 The Financial Stability Board (FSB) today published its second Peer Review of Türkiye , examining the country’s progress in implementing the FSB recommendations for the regulation and supervision of crypto-asset activities, including stablecoins.

item.title: Peer Review of Türkiye
item.description: The FSB’s 2025 thematic peer review on the implementation of its global regulatory framework for crypto-asset activities showed that Türkiye had finalised a regulatory framework for crypto assets, although not for stablecoins. The FSB recommends further steps to reinforce Türkiye’s regulatory framework and improve alignment with the FSB Global Regulatory Framework for Crypto-asset Activities , focusing in particular on operationalising a framework for financial stability monitoring, establishing a dedicated regime for stablecoins, strengthening supervision and enforcement, and promoting effective cross-border cooperation and information sharing. Turkish authorities have made meaningful progress in enhancing the regulation, supervision and oversight of crypto-asset markets and activities in recent years.

item.title: California Earthquake Authority lifts Ursa Re 2026-1 cat bond to target $900m of reinsurance
item.description: The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) is aiming to meaningfully upsize its latest catastrophe bond sponsorship, with the target for the issuance raised 50% to now $900 million of fully-collateralized earthquake reinsurance limit from the new Ursa Re Ltd. The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) returned to the catastrophe bond market in late October, with an initial target to secure $600 million of reinsurance protection from its latest cat bond sponsorship. This new Ursa Re 2026-1 cat bond will become the 25th visit to the market by the California Earthquake Authority (CEA) we have tracked.

item.title: Cat bond market primed for growth as perils, sponsors and capacity expands: Man Group
item.description: A new article from Man Group has highlighted how the catastrophe bond market continues to offer effective pricing competition, multi-year cover against a range of perils, and an additional source of capacity. All of which leads the firm to call out that it believes the market is well placed for further growth, provided pricing remains attractive to investors and sponsors. Given the scale of benefits that the asset class provides for investors and sponsors, Man Group outlines that it believes the market appears well placed to grow without distorting the market price of risk.

item.title: Montauk Point hires Whiley to strengthen ILS Advisory & Special Situations
item.description: Montauk Point Ltd., a Bermuda-based firm that provides independent advisory and strategic advice to third-party risk capital providers, has announced that senior ILS specialist John Whiley has joined the firm, where he will focus on strengthening its ILS Advisory and Special Situations capabilities. The company continues to build-out its team, and has now announced the appointment of Bermuda ILS specialist John Whiley, who will primarily focus on ILS advisory, operational and governance support, and special situations involving portfolio transitions, restructurings, wind-downs and capital return strategies. Whiley’s appointment will help strengthen Montauk’s capabilities towards supporting insurance risk capital providers, investment managers and reinsurance entities.

item.title: Reinsurance market shifts focus from capacity to capabilities: MS Amlin’s Ee Voon Teh
item.description: Ample reinsurance capacity, intensifying competition and growing demand for more sophisticated risk solutions are shaping market conditions across Asia Pacific, according to commentary from specialist re/insurer MS Amlin following the Singapore International Reinsurance Conference (SIRC) 2026. MS Amlin highlighted the changing dynamics of the market through observations shared by Ee Voon Teh, who noted that the availability of capital is increasingly shifting attention towards underwriting expertise, product development, and the effective deployment of capacity. Teh noted that the conference theme, ‘Capacity to Capabilities’, reflected current market dynamics, with available capacity no longer the primary constraint.

item.title: HIVE appoints Kenrick Aldrich as Head of Capacity Management
item.description: HIVE Underwriters, an independent specialty managing general agent (MGA), has announced the appointment of Kenrick Aldrich as Head of Capacity Management. Kenrick brings a valuable perspective and will play a pivotal role in strengthening the relationships that underpin our business, while opening new avenues for sustainable growth.” Kenrick Aldrich, Head of Capacity Management at HIVE Underwriters, added, “HIVE has a clear ambition for its future, and the opportunity to help turn that ambition into growth is compelling. In his new role, Aldrich will focus on expanding HIVE’s insurance panel and deepening long-term capacity support across its multi-class specialty offering, working closely with the company’s leadership and underwriting teams.

item.title: Data centre outage risks create opportunities for parametric and non-damage BI cover: Howden
item.description: A new Howden report has highlighted the heavy financial toll of data centre outages, pointing to opportunities for innovative solutions, including parametric cover linked to service-level agreements and, where available, non-damage business interruption insurance. “This is creating opportunities for innovative solutions, including parametric cover linked to service-level agreements and, where available, non-damage business interruption insurance,” the firm added. “This is driving a capex boom in the utility sector and concurrently accelerating a shift towards alternative power sources for data centres, bringing new operational and financial risks,” Howden said.

item.title: King Risk Partners acquires Florida agency Lott & Gaylor Insurance
item.description: King Risk Partners, the 36th largest insurance brokerage in the US, has acquired Lott & Gaylor Insurance, an agency based in Fort Myers, Florida, for an undisclosed sum. "Lott & Gaylor's longstanding relationships and understanding of Southwest Florida's insurance needs make the agency a strong addition to King Risk Partners," said Scott Popilek, Chief Executive Officer of King Risk Partners. The acquisition adds a Fort Myers agency offering personal and commercial insurance, employee benefits and specialised coverage to King Risk Partners' business in Southwest Florida.

item.title: Ancep raises $8.5m in Creandum-led round for broker AI agents
item.description: London-based Ancep, which builds AI agents for commercial insurance brokers, has raised $8.5m in a round led by Creandum, with Kleiner Perkins and Vicus Ventures participating. Ancep's AI agents automate routine stages of insurance placement for commercial brokers. Only an authorised broker can bind a policy, and broking teams review the agents' outputs.

item.title: Rebuild Capital backs Cosign
item.description: Rebuild Capital disclosed an investment in Cosign , a rental guarantor platform that helps renters qualify for housing while protecting property owners against lost rent. Rebuild Capital, founded by Jeremy Kaner, invests in real estate and construction technology companies. The investment firm described itself as Cosign’s first investor in a November 10 portfolio update.

item.title: Healthy Paws head Alex Faynberg joins MetLife
item.description: Alex Faynberg, who was appointed head of Chubb’s Healthy Paws pet insurance business effective March 3, 2025, has joined MetLife as Senior Vice President, according to his LinkedIn profile. Before MetLife, Jorgensen spent eight years at Healthy Paws, most recently as President and COO. Before Healthy Paws, he was Division President of Chubb Workplace Benefits and, before that, SVP and Chief Actuary at Combined Insurance, a Chubb company.
